subject: Re: Post-call: Structured output reliability / SDK integration next steps
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Structured output reliability: follow-up and next steps

Thanks for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and items we need to validate on our side before the POC:

- Goal: integrate Redwood for multi-step extraction + reranking. We need stable JSON outputs for downstream ETL jobs.
- Areas we discussed: SDK setup and auth flow, routing to dedicated capacity, structured output (JSON schema + constrained decoding), embeddings for reranking, and failure/retry behavior.

Requests from our side:
1) A short guide showing the SDK auth flow for service accounts (we prefer key-based server-to-server auth).
2) Recommended approach for constrained decoding and validating JSON schema at inference time — we want guidance on validator + retry semantics.
3) An example for embeddings + reranker pipeline and how to route heavy embedding traffic to dedicated pools.

Can you share the example schema you mentioned and a checklist of integration steps? We want to line this up with our Platform Ops team for a Jan-style POC (2-week).

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Data Platform
Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structured output reliability: follow-up and next steps

Appreciate the clear ask, Alex — good to align on scope. Quick answers and next steps below. Attaching a small JSON schema example and our SDK quickstart doc.

Short answers:
- SDK + auth: we support short-lived service tokens (recommended) and long-lived API keys. For server-to-server we can provide a managed service account flow + OIDC/KMS integration for secrets. Aditya, linking the internal snippet for the service account JWT exchange.
- Constrained decoding: we recommend a two-layer pattern: 1) model-side constrained decoding (structured output templates + token filters) and 2) client-side schema validation with automatic retry + fallback to a more permissive prompt. See the example in the attached json-schema-example.json.
- Embeddings/rerank: route embedding-heavy routes to a dedicated pool with autoscale policies; use batched embed calls with the SDK to reduce unit cost.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll loop Aditya (solution engineer) to share the SDK code snippets for auth and routing by EOD today.
2) We’ll provide a small reference Flask/Node sample that shows: auth, creating structured output prompts, constrained decoding flags, schema validation and retry pattern.
3) Platform Ops: if you can share a preferred SRE contact and expected QPS for embeddings, we’ll propose a Dedicated capacity config.

If that works I’ll raise a mutual action plan and timeline for the 2-week POC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structured output reliability: follow-up and next steps

Alex — adding the concrete snippets I promised. Below is a condensed reference (I’ll push full files to the Drive link Marissa mentioned):

1) SDK auth (server-to-server)
- Create a service account in the Redwood Console -> Generate a key (JSON).
- Exchange key for short-lived token via POST /v1/token (we can provide an example Node script).
- Use the token in Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

2) Constrained decoding + validation pattern (recommended)
- Prompt: include a strict JSON template with field names and types. Use Redwood constrained decoding flags (e.g., allowlist token prefixes, stop sequences) to reduce hallucinations.
- Server-side validation: run a JSON schema validator (we recommend AJV for Node, jsonschema for Python).
- Retry logic: on validation failure, retry up to N times (configurable) with: 1) prompt that adds the invalid example and asks for correction, 2) increase temperature/beam adjustments, or 3) fallback to a simpler extraction approach (e.g., regex post-process) if repeated failures occur.
- Idempotency: attach a request-id so retries can be deduplicated in downstream pipelines.

3) Example snippet (pseudo):
- Request: model=redwood-structured-1, prompt="Output MUST be JSON matching schema X."
- Param: constrained_decoding=true, token_allowlist=["\","{","}","\":"], max_retries=2
- Post-process: validate(JSON) -> if invalid -> retry_with_context() -> if still invalid -> log & route to manual review queue (S3 + notification).

4) Embeddings/rerank flow
- Batch embed requests (up to 512 items per batch) to the embeddings endpoint; use async job mode for large jobs.
- Store vectors in your vector DB (we suggest starting with Milvus or Pinecone); run coarse filter then rerank with a dedicated model endpoint (routing config in Redwood console).

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md, json-schema-example.json

Let me know preferred language (Node/Python/Go) and I’ll send the concrete repo.

Thanks,
Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-analytics.com>, Platform Ops <platform-ops@acme-analytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-12T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structured output reliability: follow-up and next steps

Thanks — that all looks good. A few clarifications from Platform Ops before we kick off the POC:

- Auth: we prefer OIDC + short-lived tokens; can you confirm the token refresh flow and whether tokens can be scoped to specific routes (e.g., embeddings only)?
- Validation/retry: for throughput reasons we prefer client-side validation + an async correction job rather than synchronous retry for every request. Can you provide recommended SLAs for retries (latency budget) and an example async correction loop (e.g., place invalid outputs in a correction queue for a separate worker)?
- Dedicated capacity: estimated initial QPS for embeddings is ~40 QPS, batchable. We’ll share the SRE contact and a preliminary infra diagram.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood: share Node/Python sample repo showing OIDC exchange, constrained decoding flags, schema validator integration, and an async retry/correction pattern.
2) Acme: share SRE contact and target POC success criteria (schema pass rate >= 95%, end-to-end latency < 300ms for 95th pctl for structured-extract calls).

If you can drop the sample repo by EOD Tuesday we can align resources and start the POC next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Platform Ops, Acme Analytics
